Dan S. Sullivan

Registered Republican candidate for United States Senator, Alaska · Incumbent

U.S. Senator (incumbent)

Dan S. Sullivan is a Republican who has represented Alaska in the U.S. Senate since 2015 and is seeking re-election. He advanced from Alaska's nonpartisan top-four primary on August 18, 2026, to the November 3 ranked-choice general election. His opponents are Democrat Mary Peltola, Republican Gerald Heikes, and a Petersburg Republican who has a similar name, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.

Where Sullivan stands

Iran / foreign policy
Supports President Trump's use of war powers against Iran. He said in the Oct. 15 debate that 'the largest state sponsor of terrorism should not have nuclear weapons.'
Energy and cost of living
Says energy costs from the Iran war are too high and argues that producing more domestic energy would bring costs down. He calls fuel prices his top issue.
Fisheries
Says he worked to make Alaska fishermen eligible for USDA fuel cost relief.
Infrastructure
Joined the Alaska congressional delegation in announcing a $249 million federal grant to finish the Port MacKenzie rail extension.
Alaska Native lands
Introduced legislation to expand the lands available for Alaska Native land selections.

Background

  • U.S. Senator from Alaska, 2015–present
  • Alaska Commissioner of Natural Resources, 2010–2013
  • Alaska Attorney General, 2009–2010
  • U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Economic, Energy and Business Affairs, 2006–2009
  • U.S. Marine Corps officer (active duty and reserve)
  • Education: B.A., Harvard University; J.D. and M.S. in Foreign Service, Georgetown University
